cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Hello?

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Oh hello. My name’s Jan. Are you the right person to talk to about the Buckworth Conservation Group?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Yes, I’m Peter. I’m the secretary.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Good. I’ve just moved to this area, and I’m interested in getting involved. I was in a similar group where I used to live. Could you tell me something about your activities, please?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Of course. Well, we have a mixture of regular activities and special events. One of the regular ones is trying to keep the beach free of litter (Q1). A few of us spend a couple of hours a month on it, and it’s awful how much there is so clear. I wish people would be more responsible and take it home with them.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I totally agree. I’d be happy to help with that. Is it OK to take dogs (Q2)?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: I’m afraid not, as they’re banned from the beach itself. You can take them along the cliffs, though. And children are welcome.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: We also manage a nature reserve, and there’s a lot to do there all year round. For example, because it’s a popular place to visit, we spend a lot of time looking after the paths and making sure they’re in good condition for walking.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I could certainly help with that.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Good. And we have a programme of creating new habitats there. We’re just finished making and installing nesting boxes for birds to use, and next we’re going to work on encouraging insects (Q3) – they’re important for the biodiversity of the reserve.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: They certainly are.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Oh, and we’re also running a project to identify the different species of butterflies (Q4) that visit the reserve. You might be interested in taking part in that.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Sure. I was involved in something similar where I used to live, counting all the species of months. I’d enjoy that.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Another job we’re doing at the reserve is replacing the wall (Q5) on the southern side, between the parking area and our woodshed. It was badly damaged in a storm last month.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: OK.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Then as I said, we have a programme of events as well, both at the weekend, and during the week.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Right. I presume you have guided walks? I’d like to get to know the local countryside, as I’m new to the area.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Yes, we do. The next walk is to Ruston Island, a week on Saturday. We’ll be meeting in the car park at Dunsmore Beach at low tide – that’s when the sands are dry enough for us to walk to the island (Q6) without getting wet.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Sounds good.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: The island’s a great place to explore. It’s quite small, and it’s got a range of habitats. It’s also an ideal location for seeing seals just off the coast, or even on the beach.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: OK. And is there anything we should bring, like a picnic, for instance?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Yes, do bring one, as it’s a full-day walk. And of course it’ll be wet walking across and back, so make sure your boots (Q7) are waterproof.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I must buy a new pair – there’s a hole in one of my current ones! Well, I’d definitely like to come on the walk.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Great. Then later this month we’re having a one-day woodwork session in Hopton Wood.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I’ve never tried that before. Is it OK for beginners (Q8) to take part?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: Definitely. There’ll be a couple of experts leading the session, and we keep the number of participants down, so you’ll get as much help as you need.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: Excellent! I’d love to be able to make chairs.

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: That’s probably too ambitious for one day! You’ll be starting with wooden spoons (Q9), and of course learning how to use the tools. And anything you make is yours to take home with you.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: That sounds like fun. When is it?

cues.speaker: PETER
cues.text: It’s on the 17th, from 10 a.m. until 3. There’s a charge of £35 (Q10), including lunch, or £40 if you want to camp in the wood.

cues.speaker: JAN
cues.text: I should think I’ll come home the same day. Well, I’d certainly like to join the group.
